latest_release.name: Hex 3.4.0
latest_release.body:
## Hex 3.4.0

> **windows, coming from 3.3:** if hex shows "download update" instead of updating itself, download setup ([x64](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup) · [arm64](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-arm64-setup)) and run it over your existing copy. don't uninstall first: settings, history and models stay, and later updates install themselves again.
>
> **hyprland, coming from 3.3:** binds to the old names with the key in them (`anomaly.hex:dictation-ALT-space`) still work for the key you had, but switch them to the fixed names before you record another key: `anomaly.hex:dictation`, `anomaly.hex:paste-last`, `anomaly.hex:capture`, `anomaly.hex:raw-dictation`. reload your config and check `hyprctl globalshortcuts`. binds that run `hex dictation …` need no change.

### new

- the first run is one story now: a bad group chat, the same conversation with hex, then your own first words
- the interface speaks russian (русский)
- new speech models: orukeet, granite speech 5.0 470m turboctc, and nb-whisper medium for norwegian. models that hear the language themselves sit under auto
- history's header is one "kept 7 days ▾" menu: retention, keep audio too, and clear all history…
- each history entry names the model and language that heard it, and replace keeps up to five earlier versions (transcribing an entry again needs its audio, kept with keep audio too)
- meetings (opt-in): names and summaries are one choice, off, on this mac or opencode (off or opencode on windows and linux), so a transcript never goes to opencode unless you pick it
- meeting rows show the call app's icon, and discord calls are detected like slack and teams
- toggle mode has its own cancel shortcut, escape by default, and there is no pre-roll when "while dictating" mutes, pauses or lowers other audio
- transcribe again asks which language to use for that run on models that take a language, and the vocabulary sheet says how many terms the selected model reads
- scroll bars are always visible and draggable on linux and windows, and menus take page up/down and home/end
- touchscreens: taps, drags and momentum scrolling work in hex's windows
- the window, hud and capsules have names, values and states for screen readers and voice control
- windows: hex.exe no longer opens a console from the start menu or login, and hex.com runs it in a terminal. logs and models move to local appdata once
- windows: `POST /dictations` uses hex's own microphone and can stream live text
- mac: the menu bar is ordered meeting, actions, then app, with the speech model and shortcuts in it
- mac: your shortcuts keep working while another app holds secure input, like a password field or a terminal's secure keyboard entry

### labs (off by default)

- screenshots on mac: ⌘⇧4 draws a crosshair over any app, a thumbnail slides in, and the editor has pen, arrow, box, text, crop, copy, save and send to. recordings save at native resolution in hevc and wait in the corner until you close them
- mac: a notch indicator for the hud, caps lock to dictate hands-free, annotate's last 15 seconds (macos 27 and later, with annotate on and screen recording allowed), and audio files imported as meetings
- up to four more dictation shortcuts on mac, each with its own activation mode, and a second one on linux and windows that uses the main shortcut's activation mode
- a speech model and language per mode that follow the app in front on mac and windows, and "while dictating" that only applies on speakers
- play kept history recordings, write meeting notes to their own file, live typing through the wayland input method, and transform typed text in the focused field on linux

### fixes

- mac: a microphone that goes silent or dies mid-dictation is reopened instead of losing the dictation, and an interrupted dictation is kept and copied instead of thrown away
- mac: the hud rejoins every space, works in the bottom position and with the notch, the live text plate no longer flashes the last d

detail.readme: # Hex Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and it pastes. ## How it works - hold the shortcut, speak, then let go - Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in - the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine - experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar ## What it does - hold the shortcut to dictate, or set Shortcut mode to Tap to start and stop with a press - the text lands at the cursor in whatever app you're in - Option-Shift-V pastes the last dictation again (Ctrl-Alt-V on Windows and Linux) - History keeps your dictations, searchable, for 7 days by default - Output runs every dictation through steps you choose (word replacements, built-in cleanups, your own scripts, an optional OpenCode rewrite), with different steps per app or website - Vocabulary is one list of names Hex should know; Whisper and Qwen3-ASR read it while transcribing, Parakeet models read it with Labs › Vocabulary help on, and the OpenCode rewrite uses it - Annotate records the screen while you draw and talk, on macOS, Linux and Windows (GNOME Wayland needs Labs › Annotate on GNOME) - an authenticated local API and the [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md) transcribe with the same model, for your own tools - Meetings is a macOS lab that records a call and writes the transcript Output and History: ## Speech models Hex downloads one model the first time it runs and transcribes with it on your machine from then on. On an English system that's Parakeet Unified English: it writes while you talk, so the text is ready when you let go. Other languages start with the model recommended for them. That model also serves meetings and `hex transcribe`. Settings' picker offers more, among others: - Parakeet v3: 25 European languages, and it hears which one you speak - Cohere Transcribe: the fewest wrong words, in 14 languages; a big download - Whisper large-v3-turbo: almost any language, and it reads your vocabulary - Qwen3-ASR 0.6B: Chinese and 29 more, and it reads your vocabulary - SenseVoice Small: Chinese, Japanese, Korean and English; a small download - Nemotron 3.5 ASR: writes while you talk, in 27 languages - Granite Speech 5.0: IBM's model, seven languages, with punctuation - one-language models: ivrit.ai Whisper for Hebrew, GigaAM v3 for Russian, NB-Whisper for Norwegian, KB-Whisper for Swedish, QwenCleo-ASR for Egyptian Arabic - more English models: Parakeet v2 and Underdog Bark 3.0 Add a GGUF model of your own with "Add model file…" in the picker; see [your own speech models](docs/features/own-models.md). ## Downloads Stable is the current release. Dev is the newest build of `dev` and updates itself from the dev channel. | Platform | Stable | Dev | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS (Apple silicon) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/macos-arm64-dmg) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/macos-arm64-dmg) | | Windows x64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-x64-setup) | | Windows ARM64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-arm64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-arm64-setup) | | Linux x86_64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64) | | Linux x86_64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-deb) | | Linux x86_64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-rpm) | | Linux ARM64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64) | | Linux ARM64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-deb) | | Linux ARM64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-rpm) | Or install with: - Homebrew: `brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex` - AUR: `yay -S hex-bin` - install script (Linux): `curl -fsSL https://anoma.ly/hex/install-linux.sh | sh` - Nix (Linux): `nix profile add github:anomalyco/hex` ## Command line `hex transcribe meeting.m4a` prints a recording's transcript, whether or not the app is running. It reads WAV, AIFF, CAF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg, WebM, and MP4/M4A/MOV, including a video's soundtrack. The same `hex` controls the running app (`hex status`, `hex dictation`, `hex settings`); see [`docs/cli.md`](docs/cli.md). On macOS the CLI is inside the app. Homebrew links it for you; otherwise link it somewhere on your `PATH` that you own: ```sh ln -s /Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex ~/.local/bin/hex ``` Linux and Windows installs put `hex` on your `PATH`. More docs are in [`docs/`](docs/README.md). ## Contributing We don't take pull requests. [Open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/hex/issues) describing the bug or idea, and our agents usually turn it around fast. MIT licensed.
